# METHOD — and why this is not a screenshot (oa-ops-runbook.md §1.6 asks for one; this is
#          strictly stronger and it is text, so it diffs and greps):
#   Each /bots row carries TWO <i class="xicon ... fa-toggle-on|fa-toggle-off sticon"> elements
#   whose `title` attribute states the toggle meaning in words:
#       AUTOS : "Scheduled automations are off"  /  (…are on)
#       EXITS : "Exit Options for positions managed by this bot are on"  /  (…are off)
#   Read from the `title` ATTRIBUTE, never from innerText and never from the CSS class alone
#   (state.md, "Capture discipline": `selected`/CSS classes do not imply a committed value;
#    innerText on CSS-rendered chips returns ""). Sweep re-run three times; identical each time.
#   Bot IDs read from each row's own `a.title[href^="/bots/bot/"]` href.
# ⭐ FINDING S0b-3 — WHY THE BOOKMARKLET MISSES THIS, PRECISELY.
#   `oa-ops-runbook.md` §1.5 records AUTOS/EXITS as "the highest-value miss" of a /bots capture,
#   and §1.6 concludes toggle state "does not survive text capture". BOTH REMAIN CORRECT AS
#   WRITTEN and are NOT edited here. What this session observed first-hand refines the CAUSE:
#     - the /bots page DOES carry AUTOS and EXITS as column HEADERS — they are present verbatim
#       in the 17:54 bookmarklet capture's header block (…STREAK, CLOSED, AUTOS, EXITS);
#     - the per-bot rows emit 18 values, not 20 (stride = 1 name + 18 values, verified across all
#       41 rows), because the two toggle cells render as ICONS with no text node;
#     - the state IS in the DOM, on the icons' `title` attribute, and is readable as shown above.
#   So the miss is a property of the CAPTURE METHOD (`document.body.innerText`), not of the page.
#   A bookmarklet that also emitted `i.sticon[title]` per row would close §1.5's highest-value gap.
#   ⛔ Stated as an observation and a candidate. Changing the bookmarklet is a decision, gated.
